standards.name: EJP-RD Resource Metadata Model (resource-metadata-schema)
standards.abstract: This metadata model describes metadata for rare-disease resources (patient registries, biobanks, catalogs, datasets and data services) intended for the EJP-RD Virtual Platform. The resources represented are registries, biobanks, datasets and associated distributions or services; metadata is expressed as RDF/DCAT extensions and example Turtle and SHACL/ShEx validation artifacts are provided. The standard is published and maintained by the EJP-RD Virtual Platform (repository: ejp-rd-vp/resource-metadata-schema), builds upon DCAT 2.0, Dublin Core (DCMI), FOAF and other vocabularies, and provides templates and spreadsheet/TSV templates plus RDF shapes to ensure consistent, machine-actionable metadata for FAIR discovery and integration.

classification.rationale: The source material provides explicit field-level templates and schema shapes (templates .md files, spreadsheet and SHEx/SHACL) that name individual metadata fields and state their ranges/types (e.g. dct:title xsd:string, dct:license URL, ejprd:populationCoverage enum). This is a concrete metadata table/schema rather than prose guidance or an ordered process.

dct:title.name: Title
dct:title.descr: The name/title of the resource (dataset, biobank, registry, guideline, etc.).
dct:title.evidence: From many module SHEx and templates: "dct:title xsd:string;" and from templates: "The name of the Biobank. This is a required field and needs to be unique."

raw_full_info.examples: Template text: 'Title\nThe name of the Biobank. This is a required field and needs to be unique.'

dct:description.name: Description
dct:description.descr: A free-text description of the resource.
dct:description.evidence: "dct:description xsd:string*;" (example SHEx) and templates such as 'Description\nA description of this Biobank\n> **Warning** This field is `required`'.

raw_full_info.template_quote: Template: 'Description\nA description of the Biobank\n> **Warning** This field is `required`'

dct:license.name: License
dct:license.descr: URL pointing to license that applies to the resource.
dct:license.evidence: Template: 'License\nThis should contain a URL that provides details regarding the license that is applicable to this resource.' and SHACL/SHEx: 'dct:license IRI;'

raw_full_info.template_quote: This should contain a URL that provides details regarding the license that is applicable to this resource.

dct:publisher.name: Publisher
dct:publisher.descr: Pointer to the organisation that published the resource (range: foaf:Organisation / foaf:Agent).
dct:publisher.evidence: Template: 'Publisher\nPointer to the Organisation that published the resource. The range is foaf:Organisation.' and SHEx: 'dct:publisher @:organisationShape;'

raw_full_info.template_quote: Pointer to the Organisation that published the resource. The range is foaf:Organisation.

dcat:theme.name: Theme
dcat:theme.descr: Ontology term(s) classifying the resource (IRI pointing to ontology concepts, e.g. Orphanet codes).
dcat:theme.evidence: Template: 'Theme\nPoints to an URL that specifies relevant ontology concepts that classify the Biobank.' and SHEx: 'dcat:theme IRI+;'

raw_full_info.template_quote: Points to an URL that specifies relevant ontology concepts that classify the Biobank.

foaf:page / dcat:landingPage.name: Landing Page / Webpage
foaf:page / dcat:landingPage.descr: A URL to a web page with more information regarding the resource.
foaf:page / dcat:landingPage.evidence: Template: 'Landing Page\nThis a URL to a web page with more information regarding the Biobank. Any URL must start with http:// or https://.' and SHEx/dataset examples: 'dcat:landingPage IRI*' and example turtle using foaf:page.

raw_full_info.template_quote: This a URL to a web page with more information regarding the Biobank. Any URL must start with http:// or https://.

ejprd:personalData.name: Personal Data
ejprd:personalData.descr: Indicates whether the resource contains personal (identifiable) data (as per GDPR).
ejprd:personalData.evidence: Template: 'Personal Data\nSet to "true" if the resource onboarded to the Virtual Platform contains personal data... otherwise "false". The range is string.' and the extension CSV: 'ejprd:personalData ... dcat:Resource xsd:string'.

raw_full_info.template_quote: Set to "true" if the resource onboarded to the Virtual Platform contains personal data, personal data meaning data related to identified or identifiable persons (as per GDPR definition), otherwise "false". The range is string.

ejprd:populationCoverage.name: Population Coverage
ejprd:populationCoverage.descr: Indicates the part of the population covered by the registry/biobank (controlled list).

This field must have 1 of the following values: "National", "International", "Regional" or "European". The range is string.' and in ShEx populationCoverageShape rdfs:label ["National" "International" "Regional"]

raw_full_info.template_quote: This field must have 1 of the following values: "National", "International", "Regional" or "European".

dct:hasVersion.descr: Version indicator (name or identifier) of the resource.
dct:hasVersion.evidence: Template: 'Version\nThe version indicator (name or identifier) of a resource. The range is a rdfs:literal' and SHEx: 'dct:hasVersion xsd:string;'

dcat:distribution (Distribution).evidence: Distribution template: 'Use this property to point to the distribution of this dataset when a distribution is available. Range is dcat:Distribution.' and SHEx: ':distributionShape IRI { ... dct:isPartOf IRI* }'.

standards.notes: This extraction focuses on the explicit, repeatable fields defined in the module templates and SHEx/SHACL shapes (the source provides many resource-specific templates: Biobank, PatientRegistry, Dataset, Distribution, DataService, Catalog, Guideline, Organisation, Location and ContactPoint). The values and ranges above are quoted directly from the templates and SHEx; implementers should consult the module-specific markdown (e.g., Biobank.md, PatientRegistry.md) and the provided SHEx/SHACL files for exact shape usage and additional optional multiplicity constraints.

standards.name: Data Catalog Vocabulary (DCAT) — Version 2
standards.abstract: This standard models metadata for data catalogues, datasets, distributions and data services (DCAT classes) as used in the EJP-RD virtual platform. The materials show examples and validation shapes (Turtle, SHACL and ShEx) describing resources such as biobanks, patient registries, datasets and their distributions; metadata is represented as RDF with fields like dct:title, dct:description, dct:publisher, dcat:distribution and dcat:endpointURL. The DCAT2 vocabulary (extended for rare-disease concepts in this project) is used as the basis; the pages include example RDF/Turtle, SHACL and ShEx validation artifacts and JSON schema exports that define concrete properties and datatypes for each class.

classification.rationale: The source material provides concrete node shapes (SHACL/ShEx) that enumerate specific properties and their datatypes (e.g. dct:title xsd:string, dct:license IRI, dcat:distribution IRI). This is a field-level metadata schema (named properties with explicit types and cardinalities), so it should be represented as a table of fields rather than prose principles or a process DAG.

The fields extracted above are those explicitly enumerated with datatypes in the provided shapes; many more DCAT properties exist in the ontology file included in the archive but were not copied as explicit shape lines in the seed material.

standards.name: EJP-RD DCAT extension (vocabulary)
standards.abstract: This resource describes a DCAT2 vocabulary extension and accompanying ShEx shapes used to describe resources in the EJP-RD virtual platform (eg. Biobank, PatientRegistry). The objects being modelled are metadata descriptions of resources such as biobanks and patient registries; the representation is RDF/OWL with example Turtle and ShEx validation shapes. The standard is an EJP-RD (European Joint Programme on Rare Diseases) metadata model maintained as an open-source extension (with code and ontology available on GitHub/W3ID). It addresses the need to extend DCAT's dataset-centric model to cover domain-specific resource classes (Biobank, PatientRegistry, service types) and to provide concrete shape constraints and controlled vocabularies for platform indexing and validation.

classification.rationale: The source provides explicit ShEx shapes and an OWL ontology that enumerate concrete metadata properties and their data types/constraints (e.g. dct:title xsd:string; dcat:theme IRI+; ejp:populationCoverage with controlled labels). This is field-level structure (named properties with types and multiplicity) rather than prose guidance or ordered workflow, so it should be represented as a metadata table.

standards.name: ShEx (Shape Expressions) — EJP-RD metadata-model v1
standards.abstract: These materials are ShEx (Shape Expressions) diagrams that define RDF shapes for metadata resources used by the EJP-RD metadata model (v1). The research objects described are metadata records for resources such as datasets, distributions, data services, organisations, locations, biobanks and patient registries; the records are represented as RDF properties and typed values (e.g. xsd:string, IRI) and the shapes document expected properties and cardinalities. The source artifacts are generated ShEx diagrams (SVGs) with links like http://purl.org/ejp-rd/metadata-model/v1/shex/... and are part of the EJP-RD project's metadata-model; the README in the archive warns these particular ShEx shapes are deprecated but they nevertheless show concrete field-level property/type specifications for the model.

classification.rationale: The source material presents concrete named properties with explicit data types and multiplicity markers (e.g. 'dct:title : xsd:string', 'foaf:page : IRI', 'dcat:theme : IRI +') rather than prose guidance or ordered stages. This is genuine field-level structure (per-shape property lists with types) and therefore should be represented as a MetadataTable.

standards.name: RDF / Turtle serialization (Semantic Web RDF)
standards.abstract: The materials describe a simple RDF/Turtle metadata model for describing resources such as organisations and locations (examples: :ErdriDOR as a foaf:Organisation and :ErdriDORLocation as a dct:Location). Records are encoded as RDF/Turtle and validated with ShEx shape constraints. The content appears to be maintained by the EJP RD metadata model (purl.org/ejp-rd/metadata-model/v1) and is published openly (site notes: "This site is open source."). The standard provides a minimal vocabulary (dcterms, foaf, optional extensions like openvoc:Country and rdfs:seeAlso) and a ShEx schema that defines required properties and their XSD types or shape references. It also includes example Turtle instances and practical publishing/operations commands for FDP servers.

classification.rationale: The source material provides explicit ShEx shape definitions listing each property with its concrete datatype or shape reference (e.g. "dct:title xsd:string", "foaf:page IRI"). This constitutes a field-level metadata specification (property names paired with concrete types), so it should be treated as a table-like metadata schema rather than prose guidance or a workflow DAG.

standards.name: Dublin Core / DCMI Metadata Terms (DCT)
standards.abstract: Dublin Core (DC/ DCTerms) is a widely used metadata vocabulary for describing resources (documents, datasets, images, web resources, etc.). The terms are defined as RDF/OWL properties (annotation properties) describing common metadata elements such as title, description, creator, publisher, date/issued/modified, identifier, type, and license. The supplied materials are an OWL serialization of the DCTerms vocabulary plus a plain list of term URIs: they list the available properties, some subProperty and range relationships, and canonical term URIs. The standard is maintained by the Dublin Core Metadata Initiative (DCMI) and provides a compact, interoperable set of metadata properties for cross-domain resource description and discovery.

classification.rationale: The source material is an ontology / vocabulary (OWL + a list of term URIs) that enumerates named metadata properties (fields) with explicit URIs and some range/domain annotations. This is best represented as a MetadataTable: each named term is a distinct metadata field (a column) with concrete identifiers and (where provided) range information. The source presents field-level structure rather than prose guidance or an ordered workflow.

standards.notes: Extraction restricted to terms explicitly present in the provided OWL/text materials. Types chosen are conservative, based on common DCMI usage (string/free_text/date/reference/ontology_term) and where available the OWL file's subProperty/range annotations; raw_full_info includes the exact URI declarations or notes when present.

standards.name: FOAF (Friend Of A Friend) vocabulary
standards.abstract: FOAF is an RDF/OWL vocabulary for describing people, agents (people, groups, organizations), and related web resources (homepages, images, accounts). The source material is an OWL module defining classes and object properties (URIs under http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/) with domain/range, labels and comments; the recording/data modality is RDF/OWL triples (vocabulary terms). The standard is the FOAF namespace vocabulary (terms and their semantics) used to annotate social-web metadata; it is provided as an ontology module (foaf_module.owl) listing properties, domains, ranges, labels and status annotations.

classification.rationale: The source is an OWL vocabulary listing named properties (fields) each with explicit domain/range/label/comment — effectively a set of named metadata fields with concrete types (ontology classes). This matches a TABLE-style extraction where each property becomes a field with a type given by its range/domain (ontology term).

account.name: http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/account
account.descr: Indicates an account held by this agent.
account.evidence: <rdfs:comment>Indicates an account held by this agent.</rdfs:comment>

raw_full_info.xml:
<owl:ObjectProperty rdf:about="http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/account">
        <rdfs:domain rdf:resource="http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/Agent"/>
        <rdfs:comment>Indicates an account held by this agent.</rdfs:comment>
        <rdfs:isDefinedBy rdf:resource="http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/"/>
        <rdfs:label>account</rdfs:label>
        <ns:term_status>testing</ns:term_status>
    </owl:ObjectProperty>

standards.notes: Extracted fields are FOAF object properties present in foaf_module.owl; each field's type is represented as 'ontology_term' with the quoted domain/range from the OWL source as possible_values.
